title: Developer RBAC v2 onboarding runbook and SIEM mapping
content:
Purpose and audience:
This doc is a practical runbook for engineering teams to onboard to RBAC v2 in a developer-friendly way. Target audience: platform engineers, service owners, and devs who will request and validate entitlements in dev/staging before production cutover. Focus is on developer self-service flows, minimal friction for common tasks, and ensuring SIEM-ready evidence capture for audit reviewers.

Why this is separate from global rollout docs:
- Most rollout docs are focused on org-wide policy and telemetry productionization. This runbook is a tactical playbook for day-to-day developer interactions: requesting roles, testing access in shadow mode, capturing evidence for audits, and mapping dev-time logs into the SIEM schema.

High-level goals:
- Let teams validate entitlements in dev and staging without requiring full product-owner approvals for every change.
- Ensure every dev-level change generates a minimal evidence bundle that can be promoted to production audit evidence if needed.
- Produce consistent SIEM fields from developer workflow events so SOC can ingest with minimal transforms.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: dev & staging onboarding, shadow-mode testing, sample SIEM mapping and event naming. Includes example CLI snippets, Terraform parity notes, and a short checklist for validators.
- Non-goals: full RBAC policy language spec (see RBAC-v2 spec), long-term archival retention policy (separate compliance doc).

Quick start (developer flow) — low friction:
1) Create an entitlement request in the Developer Entitlements UI (or via CLI). Use template: title, service, requested-capability, justification, TTL (default 24h for dev).
2) Attach a minimal test plan: a 1–3 step verification that demonstrates the capability (e.g., "call /admin-users list returns 200 and contains X").
3) Mark request as SHADOW (creates a shadow grant in dev/staging that does not affect prod).
4) Run smoke tests; capture evidence bundle (see evidence capture below).
5) Promote request to STAGED for preview in pre-prod; optional owner approval.
6) If metrics and evidence are good, raise PR to include policy change in release branch for prod rollout.

Shadow-mode specifics:
- Shadow grants are annotated with field: grant_mode=shadow and produce synthetic audit logs tagged with shadow=true so SIEM queries can filter them out of production alerting.
- Shadow grants are limited to 24h by default; requesters can extend once with owner approval.
- Side-effect guard: shadow grants should not create side-effects in downstream systems (we add a request header x-rb-shadow to API calls and services must observe it and noop state-altering ops).

Evidence capture (what to collect):
- Minimal evidence bundle (for dev): request id, requester email, justification text, copy of test plan, start/end timestamps, smoke-test logs (stdout snippets), api traces (correlation ids), and a small set of response payloads showing expected behavior.
- Format: JSONL bundle where each line is a compact event with these top-level fields: event_type, ts, actor, request_id, service, endpoint, result_snippet, trace_id, environment, shadow_flag. Keep each value concise.
- Storage: dev bundles are stored in s3://rbac-dev-evidence/<team>/<request-id>/bundle.jsonl with ACL restricted to dev-team + security.

SIEM event mapping (recommended export schema) — aim for minimal transforms:
- event_type: enum: [entitlement.request, entitlement.grant, entitlement.revoke, entitlement.shadow-eval, entitlement.promote]
- ts: ISO-8601 timestamp
- actor: email or service principal
- request_id: canonical id (prefixed by env: dev/staging/prod)
- service: logical service name (e.g., payments-api)
- capability: short name for permission (e.g., payments.write)
- grant_mode: [shadow, staged, prod]
- outcome: [granted, denied, expired, revoked]
- evidence_ref: s3 path or internal blob id
- trace_id: optional distributed trace id if available
- correlation: list of linked artifacts (PR id / Jira key / confluence id) — store as comma-separated string
- environment: dev/staging/prod
- delta: text summary of exact policy delta (short)

Notes on naming: keep service and capability identifiers stable across environments. Recommend service slug and capability slug are enforced by a linter in the request UI.

SIEM export transformation rules (ops notes):
- Maintain two export streams: production_event_stream (exclude shadow=true) and dev_event_stream (include shadow). SOC should subscribe only to production_event_stream by default; security automation can optionally consume dev_event_stream for high-trust teams.
- Normalize timestamps to UTC on ingest.
- Enrich events with team metadata from entitlement catalog during export to attach owner and product area.

Rollback triggers (dev->prod promotion safety):
- Abort promotion if any of the following occur in the 48h staging window: error-rate > 1% on calls exercising the capability, unauthorized-failure delta rising by > 0.5% compared to baseline, or any high-sev SLO alert referencing the impacted endpoints.
- Automated rollback play: label the policy PR as RBAC-ROLLBACK and run the rollback script which reverts the policy file and triggers a redeploy of the policy applier.

Metrics and dashboards to monitor during onboarding:
- shadow_grants_active{team}
- requests_per_day{team}
- avg_time_to_evidence_capture{team}
- staging_failure_rate{team}
- evidence_bundle_size_bytes{team}
- policy_delta_review_lag_hours{team}

Operational runbook (step-by-step for platform engineers):
1) Developer submits request -> validate template fields via server-side validator (fail fast).
2) Create shadow grant record in entitlement store with TTL and produce entitlement.shadow-eval event.
3) Route shadow-mode API calls to services with x-rb-shadow header. Services must be configured to return simulated success for stateful ops (or run in read-only pathways).
4) Collect evidence bundle automated pipeline: test runner calls collect_evidence.py --request <id> which pulls traces, test logs, and produces the JSONL bundle and uploads to s3.
5) Notify security channel with lightweight digest including evidence_ref and a short human justification.
6) If staged and no blockers, create policy PR with standardized diff and run repo-specific CI checks: linter, unit tests, intent smoke tests, and evidence bundle presence check.
7) On merge, policy applier picks up new policy and executes gradual rollout policy (see rollout policy below).

Rollout policy for production promotion (recommended):
- Phase 1: 1% traffic for 2 hours, monitor error rate and auth rejects.
- Phase 2: 10% traffic for 6 hours, additional checks including end-to-end integration tests.
- Phase 3: 50% for 12 hours.
- Phase 4: 100% with final audit event.
- Each phase requires no SLO breaches and no authentication anomalies. If any phase fails, automatic rollback to previous policy version and create a postmortem ticket.

Short CLI/Example snippets (dev):
- Request entitlement (CLI):
  rbacctl request --service payments-api --capability payments.write --justification "regen test" --ttl 24h --mode shadow
- Collect evidence (after running smoke test):
  rbacctl collect-evidence --request-id DEV-2025-00042 --out s3://rbac-dev-evidence/payments/DEV-2025-00042/bundle.jsonl
- Promote to staged:
  rbacctl promote --request-id DEV-2025-00042 --target staged --approver evan.roberts@redwood.ai

Sample minimal JSONL event (one line example):
{"event_type":"entitlement.shadow-eval","ts":"2025-02-11T17:02:30Z","actor":"alice@redwood.ai","request_id":"dev-DEV-2025-00042","service":"payments-api","capability":"payments.read","grant_mode":"shadow","outcome":"granted","evidence_ref":"s3://rbac-dev-evidence/payments/dev-DEV-2025-00042/bundle.jsonl","trace_id":"4f2b-...","environment":"dev","delta":"allow payments.read for service-principal X"}

Access review cadence and sampling for evidence promotion:
- We recommend a weekly lightweight sampling of shadow bundles by security for high-risk capabilities (payment, billing, secrets management). Sample 10% of shadow grants for review; if error patterns are found, expand sample to 100% for the team for two weeks.

Security controls and guardrails:
- All dev evidence bundles are signed with an HMAC using the platform signing key before storage.
- Evidence retention for dev bundles: 30 days by default (configurable per team). If a bundle is promoted to production evidence, it must be copied to the secure evidence store with longer retention (see compliance retention doc).
- Disallow accepting evidence from local machines unless captured through the sanctioned test harness (collect_evidence.py) to prevent tampering.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should shadow-mode be allowed for cross-tenant requests? (security)
- How to automate trace capture for teams not using the platform's tracing libs? (engineering)
- Decide final naming convention for correlation field (conservative: comma-separated list vs. structured array).

References and related docs:
- RBAC v2 spec (canonical): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/RBAC-v2-overview
- Evidence retention and production archival: /shared_drives/security-and-compliance/evidence-archival-and-query-patterns.json (see retention matrix)
- Policy applier design: /shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-applier-design-notes.json

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and dev-focused; it captures a low-friction path to build confidence before full production rollouts. Looking for feedback on shadow-mode TTL defaults, required evidence fields, and whether the suggested SIEM schema covers SOC needs.
- If approved, next steps: implement request UI template, add server-side validator, and wire collect_evidence CLI into CI smoke tests.

End of runbook.
